d.a: Distribution: Lampanyctus mendeleevi is widespread in waters north of the subtropical convergence in the Australasian region, from Western Australia, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria, the Kermadec Is. and New Zealand. New Zealand material is found from off North Cape to the Puysegur Bank (Fig. 4). Probably more widespread but its small size means it is not often caught, or recognised as unique. Appears to undertake a diel migration; specimens taken at night were in 23 – 250 m depth whereas those during daylight hours were in 255 – 1000 m; the former probably caught in the ascending layer. One daytime winter catch in 100 m was taken probably in the descending layer.
